name: 2D Texture-Based Volume Rendering
definition: A GPU rendering method where volumetric data is stored in 2D texture images, projected onto the image plane as object-aligned slices, and blended back-to-front.
summary: 2D Texture-Based Volume Rendering is a GPU-accelerated technique representing volumetric data as 2D texture stacks projected onto proxy geometry, distinguished by its reliance on bilinear interpolation of slices rather than trilinear sampling.
